name: Abū Jaʿfar Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl al-Naḥḥās al-Murādī
summary: Egyptian grammarian who studied in Baghdad and wrote the first full iʿrāb of the Qurʾān; the biographers tell that he drowned in the Nile.
bio: Al-Naḥḥās, 'the coppersmith's son', learnt in Baghdad from al-Zajjāj, al-Akhfash al-Aṣghar, Nifṭawayh and Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī, and went back to Egypt; al-Zubaydī places him in the third Egyptian generation, and quotes him in Sībawayh's entry for the story of the masʾala zunbūriyya as Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad told it.

His Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān analyses the grammar of the Qurʾān verse by verse, and his books on its meanings and on abrogation and his commentary on the nine long odes (al-Qaṣāʾid al-tisʿ) are still read. The biographers, Ibn Khallikān among them, tell that in 338/950 he sat on the steps of the Nilometer reciting verses to scan them, and a man who heard him thought he was casting a spell to keep the Nile from rising, and pushed him into the river, where he drowned.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 161 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
